question.text: Category II AIFs are characterized by which of the following?

answer.text: They employ complex trading strategies and use leverage
They invest only in start-ups and early-stage ventures
They do not undertake leverage or borrowing other than as permitted in the Regulations
They receive special tax incentives from the government

explanation.text: The Logic: Category II AIFs are defined as AIFs that do not fall in Category I or III and that do not undertake leverage or borrowing other than as permitted under the Regulations. Examples include PE funds and debt funds. The Trap: Option A describes Category III AIFs that use complex strategies and leverage. Option B is closer to early-stage Category I venture capital. Option D conflates Category II with categories that receive specific incentives or concessions. Note: Anchor the answer to the residual definition and the no-leverage rule from the workbook, and use only PE and debt funds as the standard examples.
